'''Peter Benedict Kronheimer''' (born 1963) is a British [[mathematician]], known for his work on [[gauge theory]] and its applications to [[3-manifold|3-]] and [[4-manifold|4-dimensional]] topology. He is William Caspar Graustein Professor of Mathematics at [[Harvard University]] and former chair of the mathematics department.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Harvard Mathematics Department : Information (Old Website)|url=http://54.172.237.215/info/index.html|access-date=2020-10-23|website=54.172.237.215}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=A Decade after FAS Moved to Tenure Track, Math Continues on Separate Path {{!}} News {{!}} The Harvard Crimson|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2016/4/27/math-department-tenure/|access-date=2020-10-23|website=www.thecrimson.com}}</ref>

== Education ==
Kronheimer attended the [[City of London School]]. He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] at [[Oxford University]] under the direction of [[Michael Atiyah]]. He has had a long association with [[Merton College]], the oldest of the constituent colleges of Oxford University, being an undergraduate, graduate, and full fellow of the college.

== Career ==
Kronheimer's early work was on [[gravitational instanton]]s, in particular the classification of [[Hyperkähler manifold|hyperkähler]] [[4-manifold]]s with asymptotical locally [[Euclidean geometry]] (ALE spaces), leading to the papers "The construction of ALE spaces as hyper-Kähler quotients" and "A Torelli-type theorem for gravitational instantons."  He and [[Hiraku Nakajima]]
gave a construction of [[instanton]]s on ALE spaces generalizing the [[Michael Atiyah|Atiyah]]–[[Nigel Hitchin|Hitchin]]–[[Vladimir Drinfeld|Drinfeld]]–[[Yuri Manin|Manin]] construction. This constructions identified these [[moduli space]]s as moduli spaces for certain [[Quiver (mathematics)|quiver]]s (see "Yang-Mills instantons on ALE gravitational instantons.") He was the initial recipient of the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach#Oberwolfach Prize|Oberwolfach prize]] in 1998 on the basis of some of this work.
 
Kronheimer has frequently collaborated with [[Tomasz Mrowka]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. Their collaboration began at the  [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach]], and their first work developed analogues of [[Simon Donaldson]]'s invariants for 4-manifolds with a distinguished surface.  They used the tools developed to prove a conjecture of [[John Milnor]], that the four-ball genus of a <math>(p,q)</math>-torus knot is <math>(p-1)(q-1)/2</math>.   They then went on to develop these tools further  and established a structure theorem for [[Donaldson's polynomial invariants]] using [[Kronheimer–Mrowka basic class]]es.  After the arrival of [[Seiberg–Witten theory]] their work on embedded surfaces culminated in a proof of the [[Thom conjecture]]—which had been outstanding for several decades.  Another of Kronheimer and Mrowka's results was a proof of the [[Property P conjecture]] for knots.  They developed an instanton Floer invariant for knots which was used in their proof that Khovanov homology detects the unknot.

Besides his research articles, his writings include a book, with [[Simon Donaldson]], on 4-manifolds, and a book with Mrowka on [[Floer homology#Seiberg–Witten Floer homology|Seiberg–Witten–Floer homology]], entitled "Monopoles and Three-Manifolds".<ref>{{cite journal|author=Taubes, Clifford Henry|author-link=Clifford Taubes|title=Review: ''Monopoles and three-manifolds'' by Peter Kronheimer and Tomasz Mrowka|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=2009|volume=46|issue=3|pages=505–509|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2009-46-03/S0273-0979-09-01250-6/S0273-0979-09-01250-6.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-09-01250-6|doi-access=free}} (In this review the misspelling "Seibenmann" for the correct [[Laurent C. Siebenmann|"Siebenmann"]] occurs.)</ref>  This book won the 2011 [[Doob Prize]] of the AMS.

In 1990 he was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in [[Kyoto]]. In 2018 he gave a plenary lecture at the ICM in [[Rio de Janeiro]], together with Tomasz Mrowka. In 2023 he was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Seminal Contribution to Research.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7137 Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution 2023]</ref>

Kronheimer's PhD students have included Ian Dowker, Jacob Rasmussen, [[Ciprian Manolescu]], Olga Plamenevskaya and Aliakbar Daemi.
